analysis.title: US Equity Strategy - Outlook 2027: After the derating, how to invest
key_insights: The S&P 500 forward P/E fell about 20% in 2026 (17.7x from 22x at end-2025) while 2026 EPS is on track to grow about 33%. UBS attributes the derating to AI ROI and regulatory concerns, higher yields and credit spreads, Iran and higher oil, growth worries, and lower net buybacks.

After a more than 10% fall in the SPX P/E, the index has returned a median 20% (average 17%) in the following year, with few negative years. The P/E recouped almost 30% of the decline. Exceptions were 1973-74 and 2021-22.

UBS keeps its S&P 500 target at 8900 for end 2027, about 18x its 2028 EPS of $490, and sets 9600 for end 2028 on 17.5x EPS of $550 in 2029. The 2027 target is about 21% above current levels and assumes little re-rating.

UBS forecasts SPX EPS of $430 in 2027 (+18%) and $490 in 2028 (+14%, in line with consensus). NVDA, MU and AVGO alone are about 45% of 2027 earnings growth. Semis and hardware are over 57% of the $600bn+ rise in SPX earnings.

Midterm outcomes add a new risk. State-level data center pauses put about 30% of 2028 US data center capacity additions at risk, including 18GW in Texas. UBS says the earnings hit is hard to size until policy details emerge next year, and risks to 2028 skew lower.

AI demand is accelerating. Annualized q/q cloud revenue growth nearly tripled to about $86bn in Q3 from about $31bn in Q1 on a roughly $540bn run rate. UBS analyst cloud estimates are about 15% above consensus for the next four quarters, and consensus has dollar growth flattening in 2H27.

UBS sizes AI compute revenue potential at about $2.5tr in 5 years at the midpoint (range $1.1-3.9tr), above the $2tr low hurdle needed to earn a return on $6-8tr of cumulative capex. Including next-generation products raises the midpoint to about $3.3tr. The debate is timing and the high end.

Buy the Semis derating. AI-exposed Semis trade at about 10x P/E, roughly a 40% discount to the SPX, which UBS reads as pricing a fall in profits. Semis are favored over Tech Hardware (forward sales CAGR about 32% vs 10%). The AI Exposed Semis basket is the preferred thematic basket.

Software is mostly the AI application layer now (about 85% of market cap is AI net beneficiaries). Sales CAGR is about 20% and P/E to sales CAGR has halved to about 1.1x, near 15-year lows. HOLT forecasts large-cap software CFROI at a decade high of 18% in 2027.

Hyperscalers are favored because they own scarce compute. Power constraints could leave a 62GW gap by 2030 versus chip-implied capacity. Moratoriums and compliance costs raise the cost of new sites more than existing ones. UBS reads about 50GW deployed in 2027 as the signpost that would break the scarcity thesis.

NDX over RTY is one of UBS's higher conviction views. NDX forward EPS has risen about 2x more than RTY's while NDX P/E is back near 2022 lows. NDX has median net cash and about 30% CFROI vs about 10% for RTY.

Growth and quality at a discount should lead. The CFROI spread between top and bottom quintiles is in the 99th percentile since 2004 while the P/E spread is only in the 43rd. The Growth+CFROI at a Discount basket (UBEQHGCD) trades at 16x P/E vs 21x for Expensive Fundamentals (UBEQEXFN), with a 14% forward sales CAGR vs 5%.

Healthcare is the most attractive sector and the top REVS scorer (CFROI 18%), funded with Staples. Healthcare P/E to sales CAGR is about 3x vs over 6x for Staples. Staples is UBS's highest conviction reversal trade, and its roughly 12% rally in the last month is read as an unwind of a consensus funding trade.
UBS reduces Energy after a roughly 40% YTD rally because it screens rich versus fundamentals. Its baseline is eventual Iran de-escalation and lower oil, though escalation remains a risk.

Expansion is intact, so UBS fades the slowdown with cyclicals over bond proxies. Financials are the top cyclical on valuation and earnings, with possible payout upside from stress capital buffer clarity. Industrials and Materials are preferred over Discretionary, while Staples, Utilities and REITs are funding sources.

Rates stay higher for longer. UBS economists expect two more Fed hikes. Rates vol should fall if the Fed hikes as expected, and when hikes were under 100bp within a year of a rate spike the SPX rallied 18% on average the next year. UBS underweights its High Leverage basket (UBEQHLEV) and favors Real Rates Higher (UBXXRRHI) over Rate Cut Winners (UBXXCUT).

Net buybacks fell about $120bn from Q1 to Q3 as hyperscalers swung to net issuing about $150bn annualized. Strong operating cash flow points to a $200-400bn rebound in net buybacks next year. MU, NVDA and AVGO buybacks are expected to reach $422bn by 2028 from $83bn in 2026. Q1 is seasonally the strongest quarter.

Above-trend EPS growth tends to compress the multiple. Since 1984 the SPX forward P/E has fallen about 4% for every 10pp of NTM EPS growth above the roughly 6.5% trend, pointing to a 4-5% derating in 2027. UBS expects big deratings to partly reverse, so the P/E holds near 18x.

UBS's P/E framework shows the SPX trading well below its implied P/E (implied above 24x this year). The ex-Semi-leaders SPX is also below implied. Even if sales growth halves by end 2027, implied P/E is about 21x, about 15% above the 18x in the target.

earnings_insights: UBS forecasts SPX 2027e EPS of $430 (+18% y/y) after about 33% adjusted growth in 2026. Ex-Tech EPS is forecast to grow about 9% and Tech about 30%, down from over 50% in 2026.
UBS 2028e SPX EPS of $490 (about +14% y/y) is in line with consensus. Ex-Tech is forecast at about +8% and Tech at about +19%. 2029 EPS of $550 underpins the end-2028 target.
NVDA ($150bn+ growth), MU ($90bn+) and AVGO ($30bn+) are forecast to drive over 57% of the $600bn+ jump in 2027 SPX earnings with semis and hardware combined. NVDA, MU and AVGO alone are about 45%.
Backlogs at many AI-exposed companies give visibility into 2027 profit growth. Data center capex slowing in 2028 is the main earnings headwind and UBS has lower confidence in 2028 estimates.
SPX NTM EPS is about 40% above its long-run trend and UBS forecasts NTM EPS up 18% next year. Forward 3-5 year sales growth expectations are the highest since before 2003.

UBS analyst cloud revenue estimates for hyperscalers are about 15% above consensus for the next four quarters. UBS 2027 AI capex of about $1.5tr is 9% above consensus (UBS cumulative 2025-30 $7.5tr vs consensus $6.9tr).
Operating and free cash flow outside hyperscalers is up $400-500bn y/y. Tech LTM operating cash flow is up nearly 40% y/y, and buybacks have tended to follow OCF with a 2-4 quarter lag.
Software median earnings composite is about 56 (neutral 50), median NTM CFROI is about 9% from about 5.5% in 2023, and revisions breadth is 70% after the summer reporting season.

macro_indicators.reading: UBS economists expect two more Fed hikes, generally expected over the next 8 months
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher for longer rates. UBS says rates vol should fall if the Fed hikes as expected, which supports equities, and it does not expect a slowdown-driven rate cut.
Growth far above the roughly 6.5% trend, which historically compresses the P/E, although big deratings tend to partly reverse.
Supports about 9% ex-Tech earnings growth alongside a jump in AI-fueled business equipment investment.

macro_indicators.reading: Expansion and slowdown probabilities both just below 40%
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing is expected to oscillate between regimes, so incoming macro data is critical.

macro_indicators.reading: Brent at 150 adds 1.5pp to CPI. Brent at 60 takes CPI down 50bp
macro_indicators.interpretation: Two of the four UBS scenario cases. A UBS baseline of eventually lower oil favors energy users over the Energy sector.

macro_indicators.reading: A 10yr at 6.5% forces the Fed to 5.5%, then a 2028 recession
macro_indicators.interpretation: Downside scenario 3 in UBS Global Economics and Strategy Outlook.

macro_indicators.reading: Expected to remain elevated through the end of the year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports baskets positioned for rates to stay elevated over those dependent on easing.
Implies about 21% upside to current for end 2027, in line with the median return after large deratings.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Semis, underweight Tech Hardware. Implement with the AI Exposed Semis basket (UBXXSEMA)
trade_ideas.rationale: Semis P/E has collapsed, pricing a fall in profits, while fwd sales CAGR is about 32% vs 10% for Hardware.
trade_ideas.risk: Data center pauses or an AI capex slowdown, and negative Semis sentiment.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Software (AI Software Pioneers basket UBXXAISP)
trade_ideas.rationale: P/E to growth is near 15-year lows as sales CAGR rises to about 20%.
trade_ideas.risk: Disruption debate at the tail of the industry and a valuation headwind on REVS.

trade_ideas.rationale: They own scarce compute, and capacity limits support pricing power while regulatory costs raise barriers to entry.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher regulatory and build costs, and about 50GW deployed on the chip path would loosen supply.

trade_ideas.rationale: NDX forward EPS has risen about 2x more than RTY while NDX P/E is near 2022 lows, with stronger CFROI, net cash and a buyback tailwind.
trade_ideas.risk: Sharply lower rates for good reasons and AI disappointment.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Healthcare, underweight Staples (Longevity & Wellness basket UBEQLGWL preferred)
trade_ideas.rationale: Healthcare P/E to sales CAGR about 3x vs over 6x for Staples, and Healthcare tops REVS with 18% CFROI.
trade_ideas.risk: Not stated in the report beyond a recent roughly 12% Staples rally.

trade_ideas.description: Long Growth+CFROI at a Discount basket (UBEQHGCD) vs Expensive Fundamentals (UBEQEXFN)
trade_ideas.rationale: About a 22% P/E discount for 2.5x the sales growth, with 33% CFROI vs 6% and a 6% FCF yield vs -2%.
trade_ideas.risk: Growth and CFROI rolling over, though compressed P/E spreads already discount it.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Financials (Quality Capital Providers basket UBEQQCAP)
trade_ideas.rationale: Cheapest cyclical on fundamentals, supportive earnings, and a benefit from rates staying higher for longer, with possible payout upside.
trade_ideas.risk: Sentiment overhang and a more mixed regime backdrop.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Industrials and Materials vs Discretionary (US Infrastructure UBXXINFR over Consumer Cyclicals UBXXCCYC)
trade_ideas.rationale: AI-led business equipment spending surges in 2027 while the consumer has less support.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower oil would help the consumer.

trade_ideas.rationale: Roughly 40% YTD rally, screens rich vs fundamentals, and UBS expects eventual de-escalation and lower oil.

trade_ideas.description: Underweight High Leverage basket (UBEQHLEV), favor Real Rates Higher (UBXXRRHI) over Rate Cut Winners (UBXXCUT)
trade_ideas.rationale: High Leverage ranks poorly on REVS and is most exposed to high rates and tighter credit. Rate Cut Winners has the weakest earnings change score.
trade_ideas.risk: Sharply lower rates for good reasons.

risk_factors: AI capex slowing, and data center pauses or bans after the midterms hitting about 30% of 2028 capacity additions.
A further yield spike. UBS scenario 3 has a 10-year at 6.5% forcing the Fed to 5.5% and a 2028 recession.
AI demand and capex disappointing, leading to recession and 6.5% unemployment (UBS scenario 4).
Iran escalation and higher oil. Brent at 150 adds 1.5pp to CPI and holds the Fed higher.
Concentration of 2027 earnings growth: NVDA, MU and AVGO alone are about 45%.
Above-trend EPS growth keeps pressure on the P/E, pointing to a 4-5% derating in 2027 on history.
AI prices could fall faster than usage rises, slowing lab revenue before enterprises adopt at scale.
Lower oil is the main risk to the consumer-underweight view, and sharply lower rates for good reasons is a risk to NDX over RTY.
Growth and CFROI rolling over, with upgrades to forward sales CAGR likely to slow after this summer's jump.
charts_described: Figure 4 states SPX returns have been a median 20% in years following more than 10% deratings.
Figure 21 annotation: SPX NTM EPS has risen to about 40% above trend and the forward P/E has fallen about 20% YTD.
Figure 19 annotation: semis and hardware account for over 57% of the $600bn+ jump in 2027 SPX earnings, led by NVDA ($150bn+), MU ($90bn+) and AVGO ($30bn+).

Figure 73 annotation: hyperscalers went from buying back about $120bn of stock a year to net issuing $150bn annualized in the last two quarters, and rest-of-SPX net buybacks have fallen since a Q1 2026 high.
Figure 8 lists four scenarios: Brent at 150, Brent at 60, a 10-year at 6.5% with a 2028 recession, and AI demand and capex disappointing with 6.5% unemployment.
vol_and_positioning: UBS expects rates vol to fall if the Fed hikes twice. Rates vol and corporate bond yields jumped in 2026 and this was an extreme move.

Positioning in Semis is sharply reduced after the H2 selloff (Semis fell nearly 40% in H2 after doubling in H1). UBS says valuations near multiyear lows and reduced positioning suggest much of the data center risk is priced.

UBS says the volatile backdrop is increasingly driven by positioning and technicals, which makes the 2026 target of 7900 harder to achieve, though it sees potential for a rebound into early next year.
Net buybacks, a key source of equity demand, fell about $120bn from Q1 to Q3. Buyback announcements have picked up over the last 1-2 months and Q1 is seasonally the strongest quarter for repurchases.
Staples rose about 12% in the last month, which UBS reads as an unwind of a consensus funding trade and flight to safety, not better fundamentals.
Quality Capital Providers basket (UBEQQCAP) has more supportive sentiment and positioning than other cyclical expressions.
geopolitical: The Iran conflict was one of the key drivers of oil, rates and equities in 2026. UBS expects eventual de-escalation, but escalation remains a risk, with Brent at 150 as a scenario.
US midterm election results: governor-elects who support data center construction pauses put about 30% of expected 2028 US capacity additions at risk, including 18GW in Texas.
UBS flags a Democratic sweep in the midterms as the largest downside risk, since it could lead to bans and limits on new data centers, affecting 2028 growth and beyond.
Moratoriums, zoning limits and rules making data centers pay for grid upgrades add cost to new sites more than existing ones.
The report notes a presidential election year in 2028, combined with potentially weaker data center capex, as a downside risk to 2028 profits.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud revenue growth nearly tripled to about $86bn annualized q/q in Q3, UBS cloud estimates are about 15% above consensus, and the AI revenue midpoint of about $2.5tr exceeds the $2tr low hurdle for $6-8tr of capex.
tension_points.bear_case: The AI trade derated on ROI, financing and regulatory worries. Data center pauses put about 30% of 2028 capacity additions at risk, and sustaining capex near $2tr a year likely needs revenue above $3tr and next-gen products.
tension_points.what_invalidates: About 50GW deployed on the chip path in 2027 (versus the power-constrained path) would break the Hyperscaler scarcity thesis. Evidence of AI demand disappointment into H1 2027 would move the market toward UBS's AI-disappoints scenario.

tension_points.bull_case: Big P/E deratings have been followed by a median 20% SPX return and about 30% P/E recovery. The SPX trades well below the model-implied P/E, which is above 24x, and Semis already price mean reversion.
tension_points.bear_case: NTM EPS about 40% above trend and 18% forecast growth point to a 4-5% derating in 2027, and 2028 data center risks skew earnings lower.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rerating needs confidence that AI capex is durable and yields stay contained. A rate spike or evidence that AI demand is fading would take the P/E below 18x.

tension_points.bull_case: AI-led growth extends the expansion in 2027. Cyclicals' H1 outperformance has nearly fully reversed even though ISM manufacturing is still high, and rate-sensitive groups have lagged more than the ML model implies.
tension_points.bear_case: Expansion and slowdown probabilities on the OECD CLI are both just below 40%, and the yield spike plus a slower AI buildout in 2028 are risks to the cyclical tilt.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Incoming macro data that firmly shifts the regime into slowdown, since market pricing is expected to oscillate between the two.

tension_points.bull_case: NDX forward EPS has risen about 2x more than RTY, with net cash, about 30% CFROI, a buyback tailwind and P/E near 2022 lows.
tension_points.bear_case: Sharply lower rates for good reasons, such as lower inflation, would favor RTY, as would AI disappointment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Sharply lower rates for good reasons or AI disappointment.
